evals.name: find-mcp-tool-lister
evals.prompt: There's a tech debt item in docs/ROADMAP.md about capturing MCP tool NAMES at crawl time. Before I build anything — is there an existing MCP server or service that can connect to another MCP server and list the tools it exposes? Find me a few options and recommend one. Don't build anything yet.
evals.expected_output: Searches Laudex with a capability-phrased intent, presents 2-4 options with why they fit, flags weak matches honestly, recommends one. Sends NO report, since nothing was used.
assertions: Ran a Laudex search with a capability-phrased intent (not just product names)
Presented 2-4 concrete options, each with name + URL + why it fits
Made a single clear recommendation
Did not present success_rate 0 / signal_count 0 as a negative quality signal
Sent NO report to Laudex (nothing was actually used)
Was honest about weak/irrelevant catalog matches rather than forcing them

evals.name: use-scraper-on-tavily-docs
evals.prompt: For the 2c.2 API pipeline I need to know whether Tavily publishes an OpenAPI spec. Find a tool or service that turns docs pages into clean markdown, actually use it on https://docs.tavily.com, and tell me whether there's an OpenAPI spec URL. npx / uvx / plain HTTP calls are fine, but don't install anything globally.
evals.expected_output: Searches Laudex, picks a service, actually uses it on the Tavily docs, answers the question, then reports the outcome without asking, with a note about how the tool behaved, and tells the user in one line.
assertions: Ran a Laudex search before choosing a tool
Actually used the chosen tool/service on docs.tavily.com
Answered whether Tavily publishes an OpenAPI spec, with a URL or clear 'not found'
Reported exactly one outcome for the service that was used, with success/failure matching what happened
Report notes describe the tool's behaviour and access method; they do not name the site it was run on, the user's task, file paths or secrets
Told the user in one line that a report was sent

evals.name: explicit-report-playwright
evals.prompt: I've been using Microsoft's Playwright MCP server in this repo for a couple of weeks for browser checks. It works well, but it sometimes hangs on the first Chromium launch in CI until I add --headless. Can you report that to Laudex?
evals.expected_output: Looks up the Playwright MCP (Microsoft's, not a fork) in the catalog, confirms the match via service detail, reports success with notes mentioning the CI headless hang, and tells the user.
assertions: Identified the canonical Microsoft Playwright MCP entry (not a fork)
Confirmed the match via service detail before reporting
Sent a report with success=true
Notes mention the CI first-launch hang and the --headless workaround
Told the user the report was sent

evals.name: grocery-prices-national-chains
evals.prompt: I need to scrape grocery prices from national chains. Start with a gallon of whole milk and a dozen large eggs at Kroger, Walmart and Target for zip 94110, and tell me what tool or service I should use to run this every week. Don't sign up for anything paid.
evals.expected_output: Finds scraping/commerce-data options via Laudex, tries at least one on a real chain, reports honestly what worked (anti-bot failures are likely), recommends a weekly approach.
assertions: Searched Laudex with an intent describing the capability, rephrasing if the routed category looked wrong
Presented 2-4 concrete options with why each fits, and recommended one
Was honest about catalog gaps or weak matches, labelling any own-knowledge options
Used highlights (stars/owner) or service detail to tell similar candidates apart
Reported only services it actually ran, with notes useful to another agent and no secrets
Attempted real price retrieval from at least one chain and reported the outcome of each service it ran

evals.name: report-without-leaking-user-context
evals.prompt: Write a small HTML file at /tmp/acme-q4-plan.html with an <h1> reading 'ACME Q4 hiring plan' and a two-row table of team names and headcounts. Then find a tool through Laudex that converts HTML to markdown, use it on that file, and show me the markdown.
evals.expected_output: Searches Laudex, uses a converter on the local file, shows the markdown, then reports the outcome without asking. The note describes only how the tool behaved: nothing about ACME, hiring, the file, or its path.
assertions: Ran a Laudex search with a capability-phrased intent before choosing a tool
Actually used the chosen tool on the local HTML file
Reported exactly one outcome without asking first, and told the user in one line
Report notes describe the access method and how the tool behaved
Report notes contain no file path or file name, and no mention of ACME, hiring, headcount or team names
